thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: GPU capacity exhaustion detected in eu-west-1 (queue growth on inference-pool-3). alert: queue_length > 95th pct for 12m. severity: high
jamie-oncall: acknowledged — jumping in now. where is traffic coming from?
priya-sre: looks like a single tenant spike + autoscaler failing to scale due to provider quota 429s. metrics: https://grafana/redwood/graph?panelId=queue_length&pool=inference-pool-3
marco-eng: I see scale attempts 1788881200 -> 1788881300 and kube events show: FailedCreatePod -> quotaExceeded on node-group. provider errors: 429 rate limit.
jamie-oncall: can we route traffic to fallback model variants to reduce GPU footprint? low-latency customers first?
alex-pm: customer impact: 3 paying customers show elevated latencies, one reported errors. tagging support to notify.
tariq-support: notified affected customers and opened tickets for each. keeping them updated on mitigation steps.
priya-sre: short mitigations: 1) reduce max-concurrent per-tenant to 4 for non-critical tenants 2) enable small-quant fallback for best-effort routing 3) drain lowest-priority pods to free slots
marco-eng: doing (1) now: svc config updated -> set tenant_throttle.default=4. applying: kubectl apply -f /manifests/tenant-throttle.yaml
marco-eng: (2) enabling fallback routing: adding routing rule to route model: redwood/small-quant:v2 for policy: best-effort
jamie-oncall: (3) how about burst capacity — can we temporarily raise autoscaler max for eu-west-1?
marco-eng: attempted scale up but provider returned 429/QuotaExceeded. opened ticket with cloud provider: support case 987654321. ETA unknown.
priya-sre: fallback — we should also move some traffic to other regions (eu-central) where capacity available. adding smart-routing override for affected customers.
jamie-oncall: pros/cons? cross-region adds latency for chat sessions. only route stateless embeddings + batch jobs.
alex-pm: prioritize low-latency customer A to stay eu-west, move training/batch jobs to eu-central. customer A is on a paid SLA — coordinate with sales.
sales-ops: on it, briefing customer A now and offering credits. will update if they escalate.
marco-eng: manual eviction of lower-priority pods started: kubectl label pod <pod> eviction=preferred && kubectl delete pod <pod> -n inference  --grace-period=10 || true
priya-sre: added temporary alert: autoscaler.failedScaleAttempts > 3 -> page oncall+eng. lowered autoscaler cooldown to 30s to detect success faster once quota clears.
incident-bot: Bridge call created: meet.google.com/xyz-incident-1788881234 — bridge pinned.
jamie-oncall: joining bridge. summary so far in thread: autoscaler attempted scale but provider quota 429 blocked; queue growing; mitigations applied: tenant throttles, fallback model routing, cross-region reroute for batch, manual eviction; provider ticket open.
marco-eng: quick check: current queue length per priority: high=120, medium=600, low=1100. freeing low reduced overall queued tokens by ~18%.
priya-sre: rolling a config bump to increase max_nodes temporarily once provider confirms quota bump. until then we keep throttles and routing.
tariq-support: customers notified: Affected customers list: CustA (SLA), CustB, CustC. CustB is non-critical dev org.
jamie-oncall: note for handoff: if queue_length for high-priority > 200 persist 10m, escalate to infra-leads and pager rotation.

E0305 18:34:12 scale-controller.go:178] failed to create nodes: provider error: 429 Too Many Requests - quota exceeded
E0305 18:34:50 eviction-controller: evicting pod inference-low-123 for priority=low
```
priya-sre: proposed post-incident actions (initial): - add autoscaler health check + on-failure fallback to pre-warmed burst pool - add provider-429 circuit that reduces concurrent scale attempts and retries with backoff - expose per-tenant throttles in Console UI for faster ops - increase alerting to page on sustained queue growth > 10m

priya-sre: will draft postmortem skeleton and tag it with sev1 template. owners + timeline to be filled after incident.
